id_and_class.summary: Edmund Husserl holds that consciousness is intentional life, the structured correlation between acts of experiencing and objects as they are meant, and that it must be described as lived before it can be explained causally. His method, the epoché, suspends the everyday assumption that the world simply is as it appears, so that one can study how objects, time, the body, other people, and scientific objectivity come to appear at all. The result is a set of structures (intentionality, inner time, embodiment, intersubjectivity, the lifeworld) that any theory of consciousness must account for.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Intentional, World-Constituting Lived Experience

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is intentional life: the field in which objects, worlds, others, selves, meanings, and evidence are constituted as appearing. It is neither a container of private items nor a passive mirror of external things.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Husserl brackets the causal question. He distinguishes the body as physical object (Körper) from the lived body (Leib), the zero-point of orientation and bearer of movement through which objects appear. Neural correlates may be necessary for empirical explanation but do not say what it is for anything to appear.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not addressed. Husserl does not derive consciousness from non-conscious processes; he treats it as the transcendental condition for anything to appear, including the objects of science.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: All consciousness is consciousness of something. Each act has a noesis (perceiving, judging, remembering, imagining) and a noema (the object as meant, which persists across changing profiles). Self-awareness is built into the flow of experience and needs no second inner act.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Husserl accepts sensory qualities, pain, and feelings but denies they are isolated atoms. The redness of red or the ache of pain are modes of givenness within a lived field shaped by intention, time, body, and horizon.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Intentional acts and their noematic senses; the temporal flow of the living present; the lived body; other embodied subjects; the lifeworld as the pretheoretical ground of science; a transcendental subjectivity reached through reduction.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: First-person phenomenological reflection under the epoché. The phenomenological reduction discloses consciousness for description; the eidetic reduction seeks invariant structures.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Noesis and noema; horizons of co-intended but absent profiles (an apple's hidden sides); degrees of fulfillment from empty intention to direct presentation; the living present of primal impression, retention, and protention; passive syntheses of association, salience, and habit.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal; intentionality; time-consciousness; pre-reflective self-awareness; embodiment; intersubjectivity; the grounding of scientific objectivity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Constitution: objects, time, and objectivity come to appear through the correlation of intending and intended, fulfilled or disappointed by further experience.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Experience is a flowing temporal process. Each moment holds the just-past (retention) and anticipates the about-to-come (protention), which is why a melody is heard as a melody. Genetic phenomenology studies how sense forms through habit, affect, and history before explicit judgment.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In embodied subjects who share a common world; the lived body is the zero-point of orientation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Husserl describes constitution, not causal function. Consciousness makes a meaningful world appear, and science itself is a sense-achievement of consciousness grounded in the lifeworld.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Time-consciousness unifies experience across moments, and the noema keeps an object identical across its changing profiles.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: The noema is not an inner picture standing between subject and object; it is the object as intended, with its sense and horizon. Perception is perspectival but not inferred from private sense-data.
core_claims_and_evidence: All consciousness is intentional, and each act pairs an act-character (noesis) with an object-as-meant (noema).
The living present has internal thickness through primal impression, retention, and protention, which makes continuity, memory, and anticipation possible.
Objects appear through partial profiles and horizons, so perception is never complete and is open to confirmation or correction.
Objectivity is constituted intersubjectively through empathy with other embodied subjects who see the same world from elsewhere.
Modern science abstracts from, and depends on, the pretheoretical lifeworld, so a science that excludes lived subjectivity misunderstands its own foundations.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Phenomenological (descriptive and eidetic analysis under the epoché).

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Husserl proposed none himself. Neurophenomenology uses disciplined first-person description to constrain neural data, and recent active-inference work tries to model Husserlian time-consciousness formally.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: His terminology is difficult and his transcendental idealism remains contested. His analyses can seem to privilege reflective philosophical description over empirical psychology.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Husserl does not solve the hard problem by deriving consciousness from physical processes; he reframes it. His accounts of embodiment and intersubjectivity were developed further by later phenomenologists.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Husserl distinguishes his view from naïve realism, skepticism, psychologism, and inner-picture representationalism. It positions itself as a constraint on any mechanism, not a rival mechanism, which lets it sit alongside empirical theories.
